title: How I'm Growing my Blog with Pinterest in 2026 | Blogging and Pinterest Workflow for More Traffic
key_points: Elna's twinsmommy.com blog currently has 24,000 views and has reached up to 50,000 views at peak times
Her other blog SpongeHacks has 55,000 views with 55 concurrent users at time of recording
Use Pinterest Trends to find blog post ideas - Pinterest will suggest content based on your profile if you've had an account for at least a year
Use ChatGPT or Claude with the prompt 'Give me SEO and clickable Pinterest titles for the topic [your topic]' to generate headline variations
AI-generated titles are often too long and should be shortened and tweaked based on writing experience
Use Pink Clicks tool to research what pins are already ranking for your target keyword
Pinterest saves are the main metric Pinterest uses to determine if it will distribute your pin more widely
Look at top-ranking pins' titles in Pink Clicks to identify words to incorporate (example: 'amigurumi', 'free pattern', 'toy size', 'easy', 'adorable')
Create pins in Canva using templates rather than AI-generated pins from tools like Ideogram or Midjourney
Bare minimum pin scheduling volume is 10-12 pins per day
Pin Generator is used for scheduling pins rather than manual daily pinning
Pinterest's native scheduler allows scheduling up to 2 weeks at a time, found under created and saved tab
Using Pinterest's scheduler versus third-party tools has not shown a big change in traffic
Focus on text on pin designs - 99% of top-performing pins have words on them based on outbound clicks analytics
Limit faces on pins - they don't perform well unless in fashion/makeup/jewelry niches
Pinterest previously deprioritized pins with kids due to safety concerns, though this has died down
Listicles are okay again after ad platforms previously disliked them
Evergreen niches can incorporate seasonal content by asking ChatGPT/Claude for seasonal content ideas for your specific niche
Pin and Win is Elna's Pinterest marketing course where she shares updated 2026 blog post creation methods and keyword research strategies
summary:
Elna from twinsmommy.com shares her blogging and Pinterest workflow for 2026, noting she's been blogging profitably for about a decade. She shows current analytics: twinsmommy.com has 24,000 views (peaks at 50,000) and her other blog SpongeHacks has 55,000 views. She emphasizes adapting to new tools and giving yourself grace during busy periods, as consistency doesn't mean daily posting.

Her simple workflow starts with using Pinterest Trends to find blog post ideas based on demand rather than guessing. Pinterest will suggest relevant content ideas if your profile is at least a year old. She demonstrates this with crochet pet accessories appearing as a trend, connecting to existing content on her blog about crochet flower patterns. She then uses ChatGPT or Claude with the prompt 'Give me SEO and clickable Pinterest titles for the topic [keyword]' to brainstorm headline angles, noting AI titles are usually too long and need tweaking.

For pin creation, she uses Pink Clicks to research what pins are already ranking for target keywords, examining save counts (Pinterest's main distribution metric) and title structures. She notes specific words from top pins like 'amigurumi', 'free pattern', 'toy size' that should be incorporated. She creates pins in Canva using templates rather than AI-generated images from Ideogram or Midjourney, stating AI pins are obvious to her.

For scheduling, she recommends a bare minimum of 10-12 pins per day using Pin Generator. Pinterest's native scheduler allows up to 2 weeks of scheduling and hasn't shown significant traffic differences compared to third-party tools. She checks her pin analytics to see what performs, noting that 99% of her top-performing pins by outbound clicks have text on them, though occasional text-free pins can still rank.

Additional tips include limiting faces on pins (they don't perform well except in fashion/makeup/jewelry), noting Pinterest previously deprioritized pins with kids due to safety concerns. For blogging, listicles are acceptable again after previous ad platform issues. She suggests turning evergreen content into seasonal content by asking ChatGPT/Claude for seasonal ideas in your niche, demonstrating with her freelance writing blog which could include posts like 'surviving summer as a freelance writer.' She mentions her Pin and Win course contains updated 2026 methods for faster blog post creation and finding Pinterest-friendly keywords.
